parsedVerdict.reasoning:
PlaceOrderUseCase.execute does application-layer work. It checks the incoming request (customerId present, items non-empty). It loads products through the ProductRepository port, checks stock across several products before changing any of them, and then calls the domain behaviour product.reserve(). It builds the Order from domain constructors and saves it through the OrderRepository port. toResponse turns the domain object into an application DTO. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP code and no framework code.

Two things are borderline. The check "Order must contain at least one item" and the stock comparison (product.getStock() < item.quantity) could also sit inside the domain objects. However, the stock pre-check spans several Product aggregates, so it reads as all-or-nothing coordination before any change, which belongs in an application use case. The empty-items check also works as input validation on the request. Neither is clearly a business rule that is missing from the domain, so the file does not take on another layer's role.
